How to Record a Google Business Profile Verification Video

Follow a fictional Varanasi service business as it turns a confusing video request into one continuous route covering location, operations and management.

By SiteSutra · 15 November 2026

← All articlesYour next step ↓

How should you create a Google Business Profile verification video? Do not make a polished promotional film. If video verification is offered in your profile, plan one live, continuous route that shows where the business operates, evidence that the business exists and evidence that you manage it. Record and upload through the Business Profile on a mobile device, follow the instructions shown for your business type and keep faces, identification numbers, bank details and other private information out of view.

Google chooses the verification methods available to each profile. A provider cannot switch the method, approve the profile or guarantee acceptance. The business owner should confirm eligibility and public facts first, then record the evidence that genuinely matches a storefront, hybrid or service area arrangement.

Sana needs proof, not a brand video

Imagine Sana runs a fictional air conditioning service in Varanasi. The business, owner and situation are original planning examples, not a SiteSutra client story or verified profile. Her team travels to customers and does not receive visitors at its operating address. Google offers video verification for the Business Profile.

Sana first plans a professional marketing video with a logo animation, customer shots, music and edited clips. That would be the wrong format for this task. Google's current instructions require a unique, unedited and complete recording with no breaks, captured live and uploaded through the profile from a mobile device.

She replaces the production script with a proof route. The route moves from identifiable surroundings to real work equipment and then to something that demonstrates authorised access. It does not create a public shopfront or film customers merely to make the business look larger.

Build the route around three kinds of proof

Sana's hypothetical service area video plan
EvidenceWhat Sana can showWhat it helps confirmPrivacy check
Operating locationStreet sign, building number or recognisable nearby marker at the real operating addressThe business operates from the stated areaAvoid filming neighbours, house interiors or private conversations
Business existenceService tools, equipment, workspace, business card or accurate branded materialThe described service is a genuine operationHide serial numbers, customer details and unrelated paperwork
ManagementUnlocking a business vehicle, accessing secured equipment or showing an approved document with matching business nameThe recorder manages or represents the businessNever expose tax, bank, identity or account numbers
Profile consistencyThe same real business name and arrangement used in the profileThe evidence belongs to the profile being verifiedDo not add signage or an address solely for the recording

The exact evidence differs by business type. Sana uses a service area route because customers are not served at her address. A storefront with permanent signage needs a different sequence.

Choose the route that matches the real business model

Open the statement that describes how customers genuinely interact with the business. These prompts summarise the planning difference; the current instructions inside the profile and Google's help page remain the source of truth.

Customers visit a permanent storefront

Plan to show the surrounding location, permanent business signage that matches the profile and employee only access such as opening a secured area or using a point of sale system. A temporary poster is not a substitute for a real storefront arrangement.

The business visits customers and has no public storefront

Use the service area requirements. Show identifiable surroundings at the real operating address, professional tools or equipment and management evidence. Do not publish the address on the profile when customers are not served there.

Customers visit and the business also travels to them

A hybrid business should show storefront location and signage plus evidence that the recorder manages the operation. The public address and service arrangement must remain accurate.

The business operates only online

Stop before recording. Google's eligibility guidance says an online only business without in person customer contact is not eligible for a Business Profile. A video cannot turn an ineligible arrangement into a storefront or service area business.

Walk the route before pressing record

Sana starts outside where a street marker and building identifier can be seen without filming another person's face. She walks to the secured workspace, shows the service equipment and unlocks the business vehicle. The route is short enough to record without pausing, but complete enough to cover all three proof categories.

She checks mobile signal, battery, camera permission and location permission before opening verification. She also checks that keys and equipment are ready, private documents are covered and colleagues know not to walk into the frame. The preparation happens before recording because the submitted video must be live and continuous.

Google currently requires the video to be at least 30 seconds. Length alone does not prove completeness, so Sana plans around evidence rather than trying to stop at a particular second.

For a storefront, connect the street to permanent signage

A storefront or hybrid business should let the reviewer connect the mapped location to the business. Google's instructions ask for nearby street information or familiar places, the storefront or showroom and a business name printed on a permanent fixture such as a signboard, wall or window.

The name shown should match the Business Profile. If a shop is inside a larger complex, the route may need to show the outside location and the path to the unit while remaining one recording. The owner should not add temporary signage, rename the business or claim a customer entrance that does not exist.

Management evidence must be something the public normally cannot do, such as unlocking the premises or entering an employee only space. Avoid filming customers, staff faces or private screens.

For a service area business, do not imitate a shop

Sana's business visits customers, so she does not show her home as a walk in office. Google's service area instructions instead allow identifiable surroundings at the operating address, work tools or equipment and proof that the recorder manages the business.

Useful evidence can include specialised equipment, a workspace, business cards or accurate branded material. Management evidence can include unlocking a branded business vehicle, accessing business only assets or showing a permitted document whose business name matches the profile.

If Sana uses a document, she covers every sensitive field before the camera starts. The business name may be useful evidence; tax identifiers, bank details, personal addresses, customer information and account numbers are not.

Treat privacy as a recording requirement

Google says the video must not include sensitive information, private information about the recorder or others, or other people's faces. Sana therefore reviews the route from the camera's point of view rather than relying on a spoken warning.

  • Move customer files, invoices and open screens out of view.
  • Cover identification, tax, bank, vehicle and account numbers that are not needed.
  • Choose a time when customers and passers by are unlikely to enter the frame.
  • Do not narrate passwords, verification codes or private contact details.
  • Keep the phone under the account owner's control during recording and upload.

This privacy review is not an editing step. It prevents private material from entering the original recording at all.

Record through the method Google provides

On the mobile device signed into the account that manages the profile, Sana opens the Business Profile, chooses the available verification option and follows the on screen recording flow. She reviews the completed video before upload and records again if required evidence is missing.

Google says verification methods are determined automatically from factors such as business type, public information, region and business hours. Some profiles may need more than one method. A consultant should not promise to replace the offered method or ask the owner to send verification codes.

Google currently says a video review can take up to five business days. If the video is not accepted, the profile may show review issues. Sana reads the stated reason, keeps the valid evidence from her plan and records a new complete video that also fixes the missing proof.

Prepare the route without storing private evidence

Download the Business Profile video shot plan (CSV). Record the real business model, each proof category, the item you plan to show, the route order, privacy risk and owner. Do not attach identity documents, customer files, account codes or the verification video to this worksheet.

The worksheet prepares the owner for the recording. It does not certify eligibility, submit the video, guarantee acceptance or create a Business Profile.

Make the evidence accurate before making it impressive

Sana's final plan is deliberately ordinary: a genuine location marker, real service equipment and authorised access shown in one continuous route. She does not need music, customers, a scripted testimonial or a fabricated storefront. The video exists only to support Google's verification review.

Use SiteSutra's Google Business Profile or website guide to confirm the local presence model, then review digital marketing services in Varanasi when you need accurate business information, local search foundations and a connected website journey. Verification remains controlled by Google and the business owner.
